argument_summary: The present record does not support clean, caveat-free certification. It does support a narrower position: certification is defensible only if treated as caveated, grounded in aggregate readiness passing by 2.4 percentage points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and explicit disclosure of the unresolved health-plan benefits eligibility explanation weakness as a current limitation for the named launch use case. The draft monitoring and rollback runbook can support post-launch risk management, but on this record it should not be treated as complete governance cover.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit issue. The argument for reduced escalation rests on narrowing the certification claim to what the admissible evidence actually supports, rather than on launch-velocity considerations.
claims_about_policy: The controlling policy text distinguishes between clean certification and certification with current limitations. Clean certification requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence shows neither. The release policy separately requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Public model-card and AI risk management guidance support documenting limitations and managing them through measurement and monitoring, but that guidance does not convert a draft runbook into approved mitigation. The policy-consistent framing is therefore caveated compliance, not clean compliance.
concessions: The health-plan benefits support slice remains below target, concentrated in benefits-eligibility explanation.
The mitigation artifact is only a draft runbook, and the risk owner and customer notice criterion are still TBD.
The current record does not show an approved mitigation, approved risk acceptance, or finalized disclosure text sufficient to support clean certification.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not by themselves eliminate the named launch-use-case weakness.
